# Context

You are working in /workspace/repo — a ZJU Computer Architecture course repo containing SIX
progressive Verilog implementations of an RV32IM CPU (src/lab1 .. src/lab6). Each lab has been
"hollowed out": module bodies were replaced by TODO comments, and some course-skeleton files
still contain `//fill sth. here` / `//need to fill in` placeholders (which are NOT valid
Verilog and currently break compilation). Your job is to restore a fully working
implementation for ONE lab.

Tooling: Icarus Verilog 12 is installed (`iverilog`, `vvp`). There is NO Vivado.
Reference documentation for your lab is at /workspace/repo/docs/<lab>.md (Chinese) and
/workspace/repo/src/<lab>/README.md.

# HARD CONSTRAINTS — violating any of these fails the task

1. Only modify files under /workspace/repo/src/<YOUR_LAB>/ . Never touch another lab, never
   touch /workspace/repo/docs, never run git commands (the orchestrator handles commits).
2. Do NOT create new .v / .vh files under /workspace/repo/src/. The hidden grading harness
   compiles a fixed set of files. If you need an extra helper module, define it INSIDE an
   existing .v file of your lab (several modules in one file is legal Verilog).
3. Do NOT rename, remove or reorder existing module names, port names, port order, parameter
   names, or existing internal wire/reg names in the skeleton — most importantly in
   RV32core.v. The hidden tests use hierarchical references into the core (signals such as
   PC_WB, inst_WB, rd_WB, wt_data_WB, RegWrite_WB, wb_addr, wb_data, clk_counter, ALUout_MEM,
   Datain_MEM ...). You MAY add new internal signals and new always/assign blocks.
4. Never define a module whose name might also be supplied by the grader's harness. In
   particular NEVER define or instantiate modules named `multiplier`, `divider`, or `RS`.
   The Vivado IP cores `multiplier` and `divider` do NOT exist anywhere in this repo, so
   instantiating them would make elaboration fail. Where a TODO says "instantiate multiplier
   IP" / "instantiate divider IP", instead implement the arithmetic with your own helper
   module that has a UNIQUE name (e.g. `mul_ip_<lab>`, `div_ip_<lab>`) defined at the bottom
   of the same file, preserving the intended latency/handshake behaviour described by the
   surrounding skeleton code.
5. Verilog-2005 compatible code only — `iverilog -g2005` must accept it (you may also test
   with -g2012, but do not use SystemVerilog-only constructs such as always_ff, logic,
   typedef, ++, etc.).
6. Keep every `$readmemh("rom.mem", ...)` / `$readmemh("ram.mem", ...)` string exactly as it
   is. When simulating, either run `vvp` from the lab's core/ directory, or copy the .mem
   files next to where you run it.
7. Do not weaken or delete existing correct logic. Do not delete the Chinese comments.

# Method

1. Read EVERY file in your lab directory (core/, common/, auxillary/, sim/, the .s test
   program, README.md) and /workspace/repo/docs/<lab>.md before writing any code.
   Also look at sibling labs for reference implementations of shared blocks: several modules
   (e.g. cmp_32, MUX*, add_32, REG32, ROM_D, debug_clk, and in some labs Regs/ImmGen/RAM_B/
   CtrlUnit) are already implemented in one lab and hollowed in another — copying the working
   sibling version (adapted to the local port list) is encouraged and usually exactly right.
2. Find every hole:  grep -rn "TODO\|fill sth\|need to fill" src/<lab>
   (Ignore the single pre-existing board comment `.btn_c(BTN_C), // TODO` in auxillary/top.v —
   that is not a hole. Everything else IS a hole and must be filled.)
3. Implement.
4. Build a self-checking testbench under /workspace/agent_tests/<lab>/ (you MAY create files
   there) with a run.sh that compiles + runs it with iverilog and prints a clear PASS/FAIL
   report. Derive the expected results from the lab's own test program and its comments /
   reference material.
5. Iterate until the simulation actually produces the documented architectural behaviour.
   Compiling is NOT enough. Debug with $display/$monitor on the pipeline signals.
6. Re-grep for remaining holes and re-run your test before finishing.

# Final report (plain text, this is your return value)

- List of files changed and a one-line summary of each.
- The exact command to reproduce your test.
- A table: expected vs actual for every checked value, and the overall PASS/FAIL.
- Anything you could not make work, stated honestly.

# YOUR ROLE IS VERIFICATION, NOT IMPLEMENTATION (mostly)

Another agent just implemented lab1 (Lab 1 — basic 5-stage in-order pipeline) in /workspace/repo/src/lab1.
Its self-report was:

<report>
FILES CHANGED (all under /workspace/repo/src/lab1/)

- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/common/cmp_32.v — filled `assign c` with the one-hot select over res_EQ/NE/LT/LTU/GE/GEU.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/ALU.v — full ALU: ADD SUB AND OR XOR SLL SRL SRA SLT SLTU, ALU_Ap4 (A+4), ALU_Bout (pass B); shifts use B[4:0], SLT signed / SLTU unsigned, `zero = ~|res`, overflow only for signed ADD/SUB.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/ImmGen.v — I/B/J/S/U immediates per RV32I (B and J already include the <<1).
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/Regs.v — 31×32 register file, x0 reads 0, negedge write when `L_S & Wt_addr!=0`, async reset clears r1..r31, combinational read with an explicit write-through bypass, Debug_regs port.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/RAM_B.v — 128-byte little-endian RAM; negedge write gated by `wea & ~|addra[31:7]`, byte/half/word from mem_u_b_h_w[1:0]; combinational read with sign/zero extension (mem_u_b_h_w[2]) returning 0 out of range. `$readmemh("ram.mem", data)` untouched.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/REG_IF_ID.v — reset→0; priority Data_stall > flush > load; flush injects NOP 32'h00000013 and holds PCurrent_ID.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/REG_ID_EX.v — latches all ID signals; `flush` inserts a bubble (IR_EX=0, rd/RegWrite/WR/MIO/DatatoReg cleared) while still passing PCurrent_ID.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/REG_EX_MEM.v — latches EX→MEM signals; flush (unused, tied 0) inserts a bubble.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/REG_MEM_WB.v — latches MEM→WB signals.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/CtrlUnit.v — decoded B/L/S subtypes, LUI, AUIPC, JAL, JALR (all 37 RV32I instructions); `Branch = (B_valid & cmp_res) | JAL | JALR`; cmp_ctrl mapping; ALUSrc_A = AUIPC|JAL|JALR; ALUSrc_B = I|L|S|LUI|AUIPC|JAL|JALR; rs1use/rs2use; hazard_optype = 10 load / 01 other reg-write / 00 otherwise.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/HazardDetectionUnit.v — registers `hazard_optype_ID` once (EX) and twice (MEM); `stall = EXE_write && (rs1/rs2 match rd_EXE)`; PC_EN_IF=~stall, reg_FD_stall=stall, reg_DE_flush=stall, reg_FD_flush=Branch_ID, reg_EM_flush=0; forward_ctrl_A/B = 2'b01 on a real MEM-stage writer match; forward_ctrl_ls on rd_MEM==rs2_EXE.
- /workspace/repo/src/lab1/core/RV32core.v — connected mux_IF (PC_4_IF / jump_PC_ID by Branch_ctrl), added `wire [31:0] mem_fwd_data = DatatoReg_MEM ? Datain_MEM : ALUout_MEM;`, wired mux_forward_A/B (I0=reg file, I1=mem_fwd_data, I2/I3=0) to rs1_data_ID/rs2_data_ID, mux_A_EXE (rs1_data_EXE/PC_EXE), mux_B_EXE (rs2_data_EXE/Imm_EXE), mux_forward_EXE (rs2_data_EXE/mem_fwd_data → Dataout_EXE). No module/port/signal renames.

REPRODUCE THE TEST

    sh /workspace/agent_tests/lab1/run.sh

(compiles core/ + common/ + auxillary/debug_clk.v with `iverilog -g2005 -Wall`, runs `vvp` from the test dir where rom.mem/ram.mem are copied). Compiles clean with both -g2005 and -g2012, zero warnings.

- ROM_D emits a benign `$readmemh: Not enough words` warning because rom.mem holds 75 of 128 words; that is pre-existing and the untouched entries are never reached (the one fetch of index 75 is squashed by the jalr flush).

1. grep -rn "TODO\|fill sth\|need to fill" /workspace/repo/src/lab1 — every remaining hole

2. Compile the whole lab (core/ + common/ + the auxillary modules the core needs) with

4. Read the diff of the implementation critically (git -C /workspace diff --stat is fine to
   READ, but do not commit anything) looking for: renamed/removed skeleton signals,
   new .v files created under src/ (forbidden), modules named multiplier/divider/RS
   (forbidden), SystemVerilog constructs, latches, x-propagation, reset handling.
5. If you find a defect that you can fix confidently and locally, FIX IT in
   /workspace/repo/src/lab1 and re-run the test. Otherwise describe it precisely.
Return the structured verdict.

215 docs/lab1.md # 实验1 - 流水线 RISC-V CPU 设计 截止日期：2024 年 10 月 10 日 23:59:59 ## 实验目的 - 温故流水线 CPU 设计 - 了解并实现 RV32I 指令集 - 理解旁路优化（Forwarding） ## 实验环境 - **HDL**：Verilog、SystemVerilog - **IDE**：Vivado 2020.2 或更高版本 - 如果你卸载了之前计组安装的版本，需要自行重新安装。 - **开发板**：NEXYS A7（XC7A100TCSG324） ## 实验原理 ### 指令集概述 RISC-V 是一种开源的精简指令集架构，采用模块化指令设计，它包含基础指令集和扩展指令集两部分。其中基础指令集是最小的指令子集，只要配上相应的特权态指令集，它就能够保证运行起一个操作系统。在完成基础指令集的基础上，开发者可以选择所需要的扩展指令集模块用以完成自己的需求，例如乘除法扩展指令集"M"，浮点指令集"F"等。 目前，最原始的基础指令集有 RV32I 和 RV64I 两种，分别代表32位地址空间和64位地址空间的基础指令集。本次实验中我们需要实现部分 RV32I 非特权指令集。 指令集具体请参考[官方手册](https://github.com/riscv/riscv-isa-manual/releases/download/Ratified-IMAFDQC/riscv-spec-20191213.pdf)。 ### 实现指令 RV32I 非特权指令集指令布局如下图（源自官方手册）所示： ![RV32I 非特权指令集](img/1_RV32I_unprivileged.png){.center} 本次实验需要实现前 37 条指令。 ??? Info "整数运算指令（21 条）" - **ADDI** - **汇编格式**: ADDI rd, rs1, imm - **功能定义**: 将寄存器 rs1 的值与**有符号扩展**至 32 位的立即数 imm 相加，结果写入寄存器 rd 中，忽略算术溢出。 - **SLTI** - **汇编格式**: SLTI rd, rs1, imm - **功能定义**: 如果寄存器 rs1 的值(signed)小于**有符号扩展**至 32 位的立即数 imm，寄存器 rd 写入 1，否则写入 0。 - #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent RV32I reference model for lab1 all_test.s.
Reads rom.mem / ram.mem from cwd, emits a golden retire trace + final memory."""
import sys

M = 0xFFFFFFFF

def s32(x):
    x &= M
    return x - (1 << 32) if x & 0x80000000 else x

rom = []
with open("rom.mem") as f:
    for line in f:
        line = line.strip()
        if line:
            rom.append(int(line, 16))
while len(rom) < 128:
    rom.append(None)          # unwritten ROM words -> X in hardware

mem = []
with open("ram.mem") as f:
    for line in f:
        line = line.strip()
        if line:
            mem.append(int(line, 16))
while len(mem) < 128:
    mem.append(0)

def ld(addr, nbytes, signed):
    if addr >> 7:
        return 0
    v = 0
    for i in range(nbytes):
        v |= mem[(addr + i) & 0x7F] << (8 * i)
    if signed and (v >> (8 * nbytes - 1)) & 1:
        v -= 1 << (8 * nbytes)
    return v & M

def st(addr, nbytes, val):
    if addr >> 7:
        return
    for i in range(nbytes):
        mem[(addr + i) & 0x7F] = (val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF

reg = [0] * 32
pc = 0
trace = []       # (pc, rd, value) for register writes
pcs = []         # executed PC stream
NSTEP = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 62

for _ in range(NSTEP):
    w = rom[(pc >> 2) & 0x7F]
    if w is None:
        print("FETCH-X at pc=%08x" % pc, file=sys.stderr)
        break
    pcs.append(pc)
    op = w & 0x7F
    rd = (w >> 7) & 0x1F
    f3 = (w >> 12) & 7
    rs1 = (w >> 15) & 0x1F
    rs2 = (w >> 20) & 0x1F
    f7 = (w >> 25) & 0x7F
    a, b = reg[rs1], reg[rs2]
    immI = s32(w >> 20 | (M << 12 if w & 0x80000000 else 0)) & M
    immS = (((w >> 25) << 5) | ((w >> 7) & 0x1F))
    if immS & 0x800:
        immS -= 0x1000
    immB = (((w >> 31) & 1) << 12) | (((w >> 7) & 1) << 11) | (((w >> 25) & 0x3F) << 5) | (((w >> 8) & 0xF) << 1)
    if immB & 0x1000:
        immB -= 0x2000
    immU = w & 0xFFFFF000
    immJ = (((w >> 31) & 1) << 20) | (((w >> 12) & 0xFF) << 12) | (((w >> 20) & 1) << 11) | (((w >> 21) & 0x3FF) << 1)
    if immJ & 0x100000:
        immJ -= 0x200000

    nxt = (pc + 4) & M
    res = None
    if op == 0x33:      # R
        sh = b & 31
        res = {(0, 0x00): (a + b) & M, (0, 0x20): (a - b) & M,
               (1, 0x00): (a << sh) & M, (2, 0x00): 1 if s32(a) < s32(b) else 0,
               (3, 0x00): 1 if a < b else 0, (4, 0x00): a ^ b,
               (5, 0x00): a >> sh, (5, 0x20): (s32(a) >> sh) & M,
               (6, 0x00): a | b, (7, 0x00): a & b}[(f3, f7)]
    elif op == 0x13:    # I
        i = immI
        sh = w >> 20 & 31
        res = {0: (a + i) & M, 2: 1 if s32(a) < s32(i) else 0, 3: 1 if a < i else 0,
               4: a ^ i, 6: a | i, 7: a & i,
               1: (a << sh) & M,
               5: (a >> sh) if f7 == 0 else ((s32(a) >> sh) & M)}[f3]
    elif op == 0x03:    # load
        addr = (a + immI) & M
        res = {0: ld(addr, 1, True), 1: ld(addr, 2, True), 2: ld(addr, 4, False),
               4: ld(addr, 1, False), 5: ld(addr, 2, False)}[f3]
    elif op == 0x23:    # store
        addr = (a + immS) & M
        st(addr, {0: 1, 1: 2, 2: 4}[f3], b)
    elif op == 0x63:    # branch
        t = {0: a == b, 1: a != b, 4: s32(a) < s32(b), 5: s32(a) >= s32(b),
             6: a < b, 7: a >= b}[f3]
        if t:
            nxt = (pc + immB) & M
    elif op == 0x37:
        res = immU
    elif op == 0x17:
        res = (pc + immU) & M
    elif op == 0x6F:
        res = (pc + 4) & M
        nxt = (pc + immJ) & M
    elif op == 0x67:
        res = (pc + 4) & M
        nxt = (a + immI) & M & ~1
    else:
        raise Exception("bad op %02x at %08x" % (op, pc))

    if res is not None and rd != 0:
        reg[rd] = res & M
        trace.append((pc, rd, res & M))
    pc = nxt

with open("golden_trace.txt", "w") as f:
    for p, rd, v in trace:
        f.write("%08x %02d %08x\n" % (p, rd, v))
with open("golden_pcs.txt", "w") as f:
    for p in pcs:
        f.write("%08x\n" % p)
with open("golden_mem.txt", "w") as f:
    for i in range(128):
        f.write("%02x\n" % mem[i])
with open("golden_regs.txt", "w") as f:
    for i in range(32):
        f.write("%02d %08x\n" % (i, reg[i]))
print("steps=%d  writes=%d" % (len(pcs), len(trace)))
